findings.title: canManage() on all-groups is granted by the VIEW scope
findings.body: `canManage()` in V2 calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. It returns true when the admin has only the `view` scope on the all-groups resource. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls `requireManage()`, so an admin with view-only access to all groups could create top-level groups. The Javadoc in `GroupPermissionEvaluator` documents the same wrong behaviour ("VIEW or MANAGE groups"). It should check only `MANAGE`. No test covers this: `testViewGroups` never tries to create a group with view-only permission.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission mixes up the resource id and the group id
findings.body: The callback in `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result. In `hasPermission`, the first argument is used as a name: `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Group resources are named by the group id (see `getOrCreateResource`), while `Resource.getId()` is a different generated id. Two consequences follow. The lookup misses the per-group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource, so the wrong resource is evaluated. The returned set contains resource ids rather than group ids, yet callers (`UsersResource` and `BruteForceUsersResource`) use it to filter users by group membership and for the users count. It should use `groupResource.getName()` for both the lookup and the result. Also, `findByType("Groups")` can return the all-groups "Groups" resource itself, whose name is not a group id.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource type resource is missing
findings.body: `getResourceTypeResource` can return null, for example if the schema is not supported or the resource has not been created. The code then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()` without a null check. `UserPermissionsV2` has the same pattern. Because these methods are now on the hot path for `canView(group)` of every group, a null here would turn an authorization check into a 500 instead of a deny.

findings.title: getResourceName has no handling for the new Groups resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` resolves a display name only for `Users` resources (id to username). Groups resources are now named by group id, but they fall through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is likely empty for these resources. Listing group permissions would then show no useful name instead of "All groups" or the group name. Add a Groups branch alongside the Users one.

findings.title: switch on a null resourceType throws NPE
findings.body: The old if/else chain tolerated a null `resourceType` and ended in the "Could not map resource object" IllegalStateException. The new `switch (resourceType)` throws a NullPointerException when `resourceType` is null, so the error is less informative and a different exception type.
